title: Chilli Con Carne
subtitle: Rich beef and kidney bean chilli
excerpt: A long-cooked beef and kidney bean chilli built on a base of smoked paprika, cumin and chilli flakes. The mince is browned properly first, which takes patience but gives the final dish a deeper, meatier flavour. This freezes well and tastes better the following day, making it ideal for batch cooking.
sourceNotes: Chilli con carne originates in the American Southwest, with roots in Texan cowboy cooking; it was popularised as 'San Antonio chilli' at the 1893 World's Fair in Chicago.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat thoroughly.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use your largest pan.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes noticeably better made a day ahead and reheated. Store covered in the fridge.

content.text: The most important step is browning the mince in batches without crowding the pan. If you add too much at once, the meat steams instead of browns and you miss the flavour you need. Work in two or three batches, leaving each batch undisturbed for a couple of minutes before breaking it up. The colour you get in this stage carries the whole dish.

Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based pot over a high heat. Brown the beef mince in 2 to 3 batches, pressing it flat against the pan and leaving it undisturbed for 2 minutes before breaking it up. Transfer each batch to a plate and repeat with the rest.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and red pepper to the same pot with a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to colour. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in the tomato puree, cumin, coriander, chilli flakes and smoked paprika. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the spices are fragrant and the puree has darkened slightly.
Return the browned mince to the pot. Pour in the tinned tomatoes and add 150ml of water. Stir well to combine. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 30 minutes.

Add the drained kidney beans, stir through and cook uncovered for a further 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened to your liking. Taste and adjust salt and chilli. Serve with rice, or leave to cool for batch cooking.

items.cause: The spices were not cooked out properly or the mince was not browned sufficiently
items.fix: Add another teaspoon of smoked paprika and cumin, cook for 1 minute, then continue. A splash of Worcestershire sauce (check for gluten-free version) also lifts the depth.

items.cause: The lid was kept on throughout, trapping steam
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on medium-low heat, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
